Quick answers (internal) — feel free to paste back to FastRetail with the examples below: 

1) Tokens vs characters: 
- We bill by tokens. Tokens are the unit after BPE-style tokenization; roughly, 1 token ≈ 3–4 English characters (this varies). Characters is a crude metric and will under/over-estimate depending on punctuation and languages. 
- For the sample payload: the prompt sentence you listed (~85 characters) tokenizes to ~22 tokens; the 600-char context tokenizes to ~170 tokens; max_tokens=180 = 180 output tokens allowed. Billed tokens for an average call (when output uses full max) ≈ prompt tokens + context tokens + output tokens ≈ 22 + 170 + 120 (assume output uses 120 on avg) = ~312 tokens.

2) Caching vs billed tokens: 
- Our standard billing counts billed tokens at time of inference generation. If a response is served from Redwood's caching layer (cache hit returning a stored completion without hitting the model), we do NOT bill full model generation tokens for that retrieval. However: 
  • We may bill a small retrieval/serve unit (equivalent to a few tokens) for metadata and de-dup checks depending on the cache config. For commercial quotes we usually model cache-hit as ~5–10 billed tokens equivalent. 
  • If the cached item is a partial completion and we re-append or continue generation, we bill for the newly generated tokens only.

3) Example unit economics and target $/1M tokens: 
- Hosted tier pricing example (list price, illustrative): $25 per 1M tokens (generation+input billed together).
- Dedicated estimate: volume discounts apply; for a committed 1B tokens/month we can approach $12–$15 per 1M tokens via reserved capacity + quantization.
- For FastRetail's stated start budget ($5k–$15k/mo): at $25/1M tokens, $5k → 200M tokens/mo; $15k → 600M tokens/mo. Using the earlier per-call estimate (~312 tokens), that maps to ~640k calls/mo → roughly 20–30k calls/day (at 600M tokens).

4) Communication tip for the AE: Translate their "characters" metric by sampling their raw payloads and running tokenization on our side. Provide a 3-line table: (raw chars → tokens) + projected $/mo at list price and at a committed discount band. That removes the back-and-forth.

I added a short worksheet to the Drive and a HubSpot note (linked). Happy to join the next call to walk through the mapping.

— Marissa

Alex — thanks for the quick answers. Short consolidated reply for you and an example calculation (we’ll attach the filled worksheet to the HubSpot deal):

- Characters vs tokens: we bill tokens. We’ll run your sample payloads through our tokenizer and return a table (chars → tokens) so you have a direct mapping.

- Cache behavior: if Redwood returns a cached completion exactly, you will NOT be billed the full generation tokens; model compute is bypassed. For planning, assume ~8 billed-token equivalent per cache hit (for metadata/lookup). If the cached item is partially reused and extended, you only pay for the extra generated tokens.

Example (using the sample payload you gave):
• Prompt: ~22 tokens
• Context (600 chars): ~170 tokens
• Output average (we estimate 120 tokens)
→ Total billed tokens per typical call ≈ 312 tokens.

Cost mapping at list-hosted price ($25 / 1M tokens):
• 1M tokens = $25
• 312 tokens per call → 1M tokens buys ~3,205 calls.
• If you run 600M tokens/mo → 600 x $25 = $15,000/mo → ~1.9M calls/mo at 312 tokens/call.

Recommendation: share 10–15 representative payloads (we'll do exact tokenization) and confirm expected cache hit rate (low/medium/high). We’ll return: (a) tokens per payload, (b) modeled monthly spend at list + 2 committed discount bands, (c) suggested cache settings and expected spend delta.

If that sounds good, I’ll produce the worksheet and a short one-slide note for procurement. Can we book 30 minutes this Thurs to review the mapping? Marissa will join to discuss committed tiers/discounts.

Best — Logan
